title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 7): The way Coath hangs
summary: A Christmas-bonus installment of NH's mocking character study of fitness YouTuber Jason Blaha, covering what NH presents as lies about his living situation, a short-lived Christian phase, and his habit of name-dropping and attaching himself to bigger YouTubers. NH frames it as exposing a pathological liar and uses it to comment on YouTube fitness's rise-and-fall dynamics.
claims: All of his channel's content is public domain: he files no copyright strikes and anyone may re-upload his videos with or without credit
If his channel is deleted he will not create a new one
He says he only discusses things about Blaha that he can prove with screenshots and videos
He portrays Blaha as someone who lies upward about wealth and lifestyle to hide dependence on others
Real forgiveness comes from the people you hurt after you ask for it, not from declaring yourself forgiven
The YouTube fitness top dog never stays on top long, and when exposed they fall hard
Natty-or-not videos are what grew many of the biggest fitness channels because that is the one thing that works
He claims he saw through Blaha immediately when he started watching him
Trolling is for fun and truthful; saying something out of jealousy or hatred is just being hateful
People who are told to dislike someone often react contrarily and like that person more, similar to demoralization where corrected lies are believed harder
He plans to continue the series monthly, and more often if harassed with sock accounts
